
This vignette walks through a complete analysis with the package functions,
from loading a system to comparing harvest strategies with performance
statistics and plots. It uses the Atlantic example, which runs quickly; the
same calls work for the Gulf of Thailand draft (`got_system_draft()`) or for
your own tables. How the two example systems were built is described in
`vignette("scenario-setup")`, the model in `vignette("how-it-works")` and
the management options in `vignette("management-options")`.

| Step | Functions |
|---|---|
| 1. Load and inspect a system | `atlantic_system()`, `got_system_draft()`, `read_ms_system()`, `plot_catchability()` |
| 2. Status quo | `ms_status_quo()`, `plot_kobe()` |
| 3. Equilibrium scenarios | `ms_simulate()`, `ms_summary()`, `ms_closure()` |
| 4. Yield curves | `ms_yield_curve()`, `ms_shared_q_curve()`, `plot_yield_curves()` |
| 5. Safeguarded MMSY | `ms_optimise()` |
| 6. Harvest strategies | `hcr_effort()`, `ms_simulate()` |
| 7. Performance statistics | `ms_perf()`, `ms_perf_table()`, `plot_bps()`, `plot_tradeoffs()`, `plot_quilt()` |
| 8. Projections | `plot_projection()`, `plot_fleet()` |
| 9. Tuning triggers | `ms_tune_hcr()` |
| 10. The app | `run_app()` |

```{r}
library(mmsyFM)
```

## 1. Load and inspect a system

A system holds the stocks, metiers (a fishing tactic on a ground), their
catchability, and the fleet segments.

```{r}
sys <- atlantic_system()
sys
```

The catchability matrix decides who catches what: each column is scaled to
the stock's highest catchability.

```{r, fig.height = 3.6}
plot_catchability(sys)
```

Your own system is read from four CSV tables with
`read_ms_system(folder, prefix)` (see `?ms_system`).

## 2. The status quo

The status quo is the open-access equilibrium: each segment fishes the days
of its vessels that break even, up to its capacity. `gamma` is the strength
of the profit preference (how strongly fishers chase the most profitable
metiers).

```{r}
sq <- ms_status_quo(sys, capacity = 1000, gamma = 1.5, years = 300)
round(sq$E_seg)                       # days by segment
round(sq$BBmsy, 2)                    # stock status
sq$summary[, c("yield", "revenue", "profit")]
```

The Kobe plot shows the stocks on the harvest-rule zones (Blim 0.25, Bpa 0.5,
trigger 0.8 Bmsy, minimum F 0.1). In equilibrium every stock lies on the
line B/Bmsy + F/Fmsy = 2.

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
plot_kobe(list("Status quo" = sq), sys)
```

## 3. Equilibrium scenarios

`ms_simulate()` runs any number of scenarios (rows of `caps`, days by
segment) in one call; `ms_summary()` gives the equilibrium yield, profit and
status. Here: the status quo, the demersal fleet halved, and the shallow reef
closed from January to June with `ms_closure()`.

```{r}
caps <- rbind(sq$E_seg, sq$E_seg * c(0.5, 1, 1))
x <- ms_simulate(sys, caps, years = 200, capacity = caps, gamma = 1.5)
s <- ms_summary(x)
cbind(scenario = c("status quo", "demersal halved"), s[, c("yield", "profit", "min_BBmsy")])

reef <- ms_closure(sys, "Reef_shallow", months = 1:6)
y <- ms_simulate(sys, matrix(sq$E_seg, 1), years = 200, capacity = matrix(sq$E_seg, 1),
                 gamma = 1.5, open = reef)
round(attr(ms_summary(y), "BBmsy")[1, ], 2)
```

## 4. Yield curves

Scaling the status-quo days up and down shows equilibrium yield over effort.
Comparing treatments shows what fleet behaviour changes:

```{r}
mult <- c(0, 10^seq(-1.5, log10(4), length.out = 25))
no_reef <- as.numeric(sys$metiers$name != "Reef_shallow")
curves <- list(
  "Shared q" = ms_shared_q_curve(sys, sq),
  "Profit-seeking" = ms_yield_curve(sys, sq$E_seg, mult, years = 150, gamma = 1.5),
  "Profit-seeking, reef closed" = ms_yield_curve(sys, sq$E_seg, mult, years = 150, gamma = 1.5, open = no_reef))
plot_yield_curves(curves, ref = sq, sys = sys)
```

* **Shared q** (one effort pool, fixed catchability) gives the classic dome.
* **Profit-seeking fleets** flatten it: effort leaves depleted stocks, but the
  choke stock (Dentex, on the shallow reef) erodes underneath.
* **Closing the shallow reef** protects the choke stock directly.

## 5. Safeguarded MMSY

`ms_optimise()` finds the effort caps that maximise equilibrium yield (or
revenue, profit, or the catch of one stock) with every stock at or above
Bpa = 0.5 Bmsy. With caps by segment, cuts can target the fleet that drives
the choke stock.

```{r}
opt <- ms_optimise(sys, "yield", levers = names(sys$segments), upper = 1000,
                   gamma = 1.5, years = 100, n = 7, zoom = 3)   # coarse grid for speed
round(opt$caps)                       # days by segment
c(yield = round(opt$summary$yield), status_quo = round(sq$summary$yield))
opt$binding                           # the choke stock(s)
```

The objective can also be a single stock, e.g. the albacore catch:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ms_optimise(sys, "ALB", levers = names(sys$segments), upper = 1000, gamma = 1.5)
```

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plot_kobe(list("Status quo" = sq, "Safeguarded MMSY" = opt), sys)
```

## 6. Harvest strategies

`hcr_effort()` builds a feedback rule: every year each segment's days are a
fraction of its full effort (here the safeguarded-MMSY days), from the
assessed status of the stocks it fishes (with error and a 2-year data lag):
full effort above the trigger (0.5 Bmsy), down to a minimum effort (10%) at
Blim, changing by at most 20% a year. Rules run in closed loop with
`ms_simulate(hcr = )`, here with process error (scaled by r and depletion as
in JABBA), implementation error and effort noise, and the same random draws
for every rule.

```{r}
n <- 60
B0 <- matrix(sq$B, n, sys$S, byrow = TRUE)
E0 <- matrix(sq$E_seg, n, sys$G, byrow = TRUE)
Em <- matrix(opt$caps, n, sys$G, byrow = TRUE)
run <- function(caps, hcr = NULL, open = 1)
  ms_simulate(sys, caps, 40, gamma = 1.5, B_init = B0, E_init = E0, capacity = 1000, hcr = hcr,
              open = open, proc_sd = proc_sd_from_r(sys$r), proc_dep = "jabba", proc_center = "median",
              rho = 0.3, impl_cv = 0.1, effort_cv = 0.1, seed = 1, keep = "all")
rule <- function(...) hcr_effort(sys, max_change = 0.2, ...)
runs <- list(
  "No control"           = run(matrix(1000, n, sys$G)),
  "Fixed MMSY effort"    = run(Em),
  "HCR value-weighted"   = run(Em, rule()),
  "HCR weakest link"     = run(Em, rule(aggregate = "min")),
  "HCR + reef closure"   = run(Em, rule(), open = ms_closure(sys, "Reef_shallow", months = 1:6)))
```

Other options of `hcr_effort()`: triggers by segment (`Btrig = c(pelagic =
0.8)`), a closure triggered by a stock (`close = "Dentex dentex"`), indicator
species (`assessed`), species complexes (`complexes`) and the nominal
assignment of stocks to fleets (`assign`).

## 7. Performance statistics

`ms_perf()` computes statistics per iteration over the evaluation years, by
stock, by segment and for the whole system, as a long `data.table` in the
format of the FLR package mseviz (so it can also be passed to
`mseviz::plotBPs()` or `mseviz::perfTable()`).

```{r}
pf <- ms_perf(runs, years = 21:40)
head(pf)
```

The statistics (`ms_statistics()`):

```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(ms_statistics()[, c("statistic", "desc", "type")])
```

A summary table (medians with 10th-90th percentiles; means for
probabilities):

```{r}
ms_perf_table(pf, c("C", "Profit", "Days", "NBpa", "PanyBlim", "AAVC"))
```

Boxplots by rule, for the system and for selected stocks (targets in green,
limits in red):

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_bps(pf, c("C", "Profit", "Days", "AAVC", "NBpa", "PanyBlim"))
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot_bps(pf, c("BBmsy", "FFmsy", "CMSY", "PBlim", "PB80"), biol = c("DEC", "SBR", "AMB"))
```

Trade-offs between catch and the other statistics:

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_tradeoffs(pf, x = "C", y = c("Profit", "NBpa", "PanyBlim", "AAVC"))
```

Colour-coded decision tables: rules x statistics (green = best, red = worst
in each column), and stocks x rules for one statistic with risk classes:

```{r, fig.height = 3}
plot_quilt(pf, c("C", "Rev", "Profit", "Days", "AAVC", "NBpa", "PanyBlim", "minBBmsy"))
```

```{r, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 8}
plot_quilt(pf, layout = "stocks", statistic = "PBpa", risk = 0.1)
```

## 8. Projections

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot_projection(runs[c("No control", "HCR value-weighted", "HCR weakest link")], "BBmsy")
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_fleet(runs[c("No control", "Fixed MMSY effort", "HCR value-weighted", "HCR weakest link")])
```

All runs start from the same year-0 state (the status quo); the rules phase
in their cuts at most 20% a year.

## 9. Tuning triggers

`ms_tune_hcr()` runs a grid of triggers with common random numbers and keeps
the highest-yield trigger whose risk meets a limit (by default: the worst
stock below Bpa at most 5% of the time):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tu <- ms_tune_hcr(sys, triggers = seq(0.3, 1, 0.1), E_ref = opt$caps, E_init = sq$E_seg,
                  B_init = sq$B, max_change = 0.2, gamma = 1.5, capacity = 1000,
                  proc_sd = proc_sd_from_r(sys$r), proc_dep = "jabba", proc_center = "median")
tu$best
```

## 10. The app

All of these steps are available interactively:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_app()
```
